summary: Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʻi, and Harvard. He taught at UC Berkeley from circa 1947 to 1984 and served as president of the American Oriental Society (1975–1976).

Edward H. Spieker worked in linguistics, Indology, and other fields. After completing his A.B. and Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins University, he served there as Associate Professor of Greek and Latin from 1880 to 1918.

Edward Hamilton Johnston was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at New College, Oxford, and under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1909–1922) and became Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit in 1937.

Edward Henry Palmer worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Sayyid Abdallah and at St John's College, Cambridge, later serving as Lord Almoner’s Professor of Arabic at Cambridge (1871–1881).
Edward Hincks was a scholar in linguistics and history and archaeology. He was educated at Midleton College and earned his B.A. from Trinity College Dublin between 1807 and 1812.

Edward James Rapson specialized in Indology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying under Cecil Bendall and Edward Byles Cowell. He held posts at the British Museum, UCL, and as Cambridge's Professor of Sanskrit (1906–1936).

Edward John Thompson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Richmond College, taught at Bankura Christian College starting in 1910, became University Lecturer in Bengali at Oxford in 1923, and was a Research Fellow at Oriel College (1936–1940).

Edward Joseph Thomas specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of St Andrews under John Burnet and at Cambridge. He served as Head of the Oriental Languages Department and Librarian at Cambridge University Library (~1909–1950).

Edward Kamens is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at Yale University (~1974–1982) and served on its faculty from 1986 to 2022, retiring as Sumitomo Professor Emeritus of East Asian Languages & Literatures.

Edward Klich was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Jagiellonian University under Jan Michał Rozwadowski between circa 1900 and 1904, and later became a professor at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań in 1929.
Edward Lavallin Puxley was active in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Brasenose College, Oxford, in 1852 and served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from 1859 to 1866.

Edward Lucas Hogarth was an Indology scholar who earned his B.A. and M.A. at Brasenose College, Oxford. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Oxford and served as Head Master at the Government Provincial School, Calicut (~1866–1870).
Edward Payson Newton was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed his studies at Princeton University (~1866–1870) and Pittsburgh Theological Seminary (~1870–1873).
Edward Peter Rice was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Cheshunt College and the University of London, and worked with the London Missionary Society from 1873 to 1915.

Edward Rehatsek worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology after studying at Eötvös Loránd University. He held professorships at the University of Breslau and Wilson College, Mumbai, and served as an examiner for the University of Mumbai.

Edward Ross works in Buddhist studies, computational studies, and religious studies. He studied at McGill University, the University of Hong Kong, and the University of Reading, where he served as an Associate Lecturer from 2020 to 2025.

Edward Russell Ayrton was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at St Paul's School, trained under Flinders Petrie, and held an archaeological post at Abydos from circa 1902 to 1904.

Edward S. Casey is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Northwestern, and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at Yale, served as Dean of the Philosophical Faculty at Stony Brook (~1978), and was APA president (2009–2010).

Linguist Edward Sapir studied at Columbia University under Franz Boas and Wilhelm Wundt. He headed anthropology at the Geological Survey of Canada (1910–1925), taught at the University of Chicago, and became Sterling Professor at Yale in 1931.
Edward Thomas was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at East India Company College (~1830–1832) and served as a writer in the Bengal Civil Service from 1832 to 1857.
